name: Ground Turkey Stir Fry Bowls
ingredients: Yellow Onion: 1 medium sweet onion, diced (385 g)
Green Onions: 3, green parts sliced (90 g)
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Add the sliced zucchini and green peppers and stir fry until they are just tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, teriyaki sauce, honey, and a dash of hot sauce.
Let it bubble a couple minutes so the sauce coats everything and thickens slightly.
Serve it hot over cooked white rice.
head_steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Add the sliced zucchini and green peppers and stir fry until they are just tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, teriyaki sauce, honey, and a dash of hot sauce.
Let it bubble a couple minutes so the sauce coats everything and thickens slightly.
Serve it hot over cooked white rice.

findings.detail: Costed but never used in the steps; the source sautes the diced onion as the aromatic base of the stir fry.
Costed but never used; the source sautes celery with the onion for 5 minutes before the turkey goes in.

findings.detail: Costed but never used in any step; the source finishes the bowls with sliced green onions.
Costed but never used; the source's teriyaki sauce includes 2 tsp toasted sesame oil.
Costed but never used; the source's teriyaki sauce includes 1 tbsp vinegar. Same defect family as the General Tso card.

name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 4.25 lb (1890 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Bring a big pot of chicken broth to a bare simmer with a few smashed ginger slices and green onion tops. It should barely move, with a bubble breaking every second or two. A rolling boil makes chicken rubbery.

Lower the chicken breasts in and poach gently until just cooked through, about 15 minutes depending on thickness. Pull them out and drop them straight into ice water for 5 minutes, which stops the cooking and firms up the texture.
Skim the fat off the top of the broth and reserve every drop of the liquid.
Melt the butter with some of the vegetable oil in a pot, fry the minced garlic and ginger until fragrant, add the rinsed rice, and toast it for two minutes.
Pour in the reserved poaching broth, bring it to a boil, then cover and cook on low until the rice is done, about 18 minutes. Rest it covered for 10 minutes more.

Make the sauces while the rice cooks. Blend the rest of the ginger and garlic with the remaining vegetable oil, salt, and lime juice for the ginger garlic sauce, and stir the soy sauce with the sugar for the dark sauce. Blend the jalapeno with a little of each for the chili sauce.
Slice the chilled chicken thick across the grain.
head_steps: Poach the chicken gently in seasoned broth, then shock it in ice water.
Skim and reserve all the poaching broth.
Fry garlic and ginger in butter and oil, toast the rinsed rice, then cook it in the reserved broth.
Blend the ginger garlic sauce, mix the sweet soy sauce, and blend the chili sauce.
Slice the chilled chicken and weigh rice and chicken into 14 containers with sauces on the side.

findings.detail: Costed but never used; the source's chili sauce includes sesame oil, and our chili-sauce step only blends jalapeno 'with a little of each' of the other two sauces.
Costed but never used; the source's chili sauce includes 1/2 tsp rice vinegar which our sauce steps drop.
Costed but no step uses it or says 'season'.

name: Ham and White Bean Soup
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, carrots and celery, and drain and rinse the white beans.
Heat a large pot and cook the diced ham until the edges brown and it renders a little fat. Browning the ham first is what gives this soup its backbone.
Add the onion, carrots and celery to the pot and cook until they soften and pick up the browned bits.
Stir in the chili powder, dried parsley, black pepper and bay leaves and cook for a minute.
Pour in the chicken broth and the diced tomatoes and bring everything up to a simmer.
Add the drained white beans and simmer gently, mashing a scoop of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth naturally.
Pull the bay leaves, taste for salt, and cook the rice separately to serve it under the soup.
head_steps: Brown the diced ham in a large pot until the edges color.
Add the diced onion, carrots and celery and cook until softened.
Stir in the chili powder, parsley, black pepper and bay leaves.
Add the chicken broth and diced tomatoes and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the drained white beans, mash some against the pot to thicken, and serve over cooked rice.

findings.detail: Steps say 'stir in ... bay leaves' and later 'Pull the bay leaves' but bay leaves are not in the costed list (the source recipe also has none).

name: Ham Fried Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice the day before if you can and spread it on a sheet pan to cool and dry in the fridge overnight.
Dice the carrots small, slice the green onions and separate the white parts from the green tops, and mince the garlic.
Beat the eggs, then scramble them in a little of the vegetable oil in your largest skillet until just set. Take them out and chop them roughly.
Add more oil and fry the diced ham until the edges crisp, then add the carrots and the white parts of the green onions and cook until the carrots soften.
Add the garlic for a few seconds, then add the cold rice and press it into the hot pan. Let it sit undisturbed between stirs so it toasts instead of steaming.
Pour the soy sauce around the edges of the pan rather than into the middle so it hits hot metal and caramelizes.
Kill the heat, fold in the scrambled egg and the green onion tops, then finish with the sesame oil and black pepper.
head_steps: Cook the rice ahead and chill it so it dries out before frying.
Scramble the beaten eggs in a little oil, then remove and chop them.
Fry the diced ham until crisp at the edges, then add carrots and the white parts of the green onions.
Add the garlic, then the cold rice, pressing it into the hot pan so it toasts.
Pour the soy sauce around the pan edges, fold in the egg and green onion tops, and finish with sesame oil.

findings.detail: Salt is costed but no step uses it or says 'season' (the source recipe uses no added salt either).

name: Harissa Chicken Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1667 g)
Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7.5 oz (210 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Cube the chicken breast and toss it with the harissa paste, a third of the lime juice, salt, garlic powder, cumin, and onion powder.
Sear the chicken in a hot skillet in batches, 6 to 8 minutes per batch, until it reaches 165F inside. Crowding the pan steams it, so give it room.
Whisk the tahini, Greek yogurt, remaining lime juice, and a splash of water into a pourable sauce. Season with salt.
Warm the frozen peas, and dice the cucumber and red onion.
Portion rice into 14 containers, add chicken and peas, then top with cucumber, red onion, feta, and the tahini sauce kept to one side.
head_steps: Cook the rice and set aside.
Toss cubed chicken with harissa, lime, and spices, then sear in batches to 165F.
Whisk tahini, Greek yogurt, lime juice, and water into a sauce.
Portion rice, chicken, and peas into 14 containers; top with cucumber, red onion, feta, and sauce.

findings.detail: Costed but never used; both the chicken rub and tahini sauce steps season with salt only, matching the source which uses no black pepper.

name: Honey Garlic Steak Bites and Potatoes
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (2 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the sirloin into even bite sized cubes and season them with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Sear the cubes in the vegetable oil in batches over high heat, just long enough to brown the outside. They should still be rare in the middle.
Move the seared beef to the slow cooker with any browned bits from the pan.
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, and minced garlic together and pour it over the beef.
Cover and cook on low for 3 hours, until the cubes are tender but still holding their shape.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little cold water, stir it in, and cook on high 15 minutes until the glaze coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the butter off the heat so the glaze goes glossy, then taste for salt.
head_steps: Cut the sirloin into even cubes and season with salt, pepper, and chili flakes.
Sear the cubes in batches over high heat, browning the outside only.
Slow cook on low 3 hours in honey, soy sauce, and garlic.
Stir in a cornstarch slurry and thicken on high 15 minutes.
Finish with butter off the heat and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: The card is titled '...and Potatoes' and buys 2.1 kg of potatoes, but no step ever cooks or serves them; the source recipe contains no potatoes at all (they were our addition that never got a step).

name: Japanese Turkey Nikujaga (Meat and Potato Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the turkey breast into thin strips. Thin is important, because strips soak up the broth while chunks just sit in it.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into large chunks, slice the carrots on a diagonal, and cut the onion into thick wedges.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy pot and sear the turkey strips until they lose their pink, then add the onion wedges and cook 3 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrots, then pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. The liquid should come most of the way up the vegetables but not drown them.
Bring it to a simmer, then lay a round of parchment right on the surface and cover the pot. That paper lid is the Japanese trick that keeps everything basted without boiling the potatoes apart.
Simmer on low for 25 to 30 minutes until the potatoes are fork tender and the turkey has reached 165F, shaking the pot instead of stirring so nothing breaks up.
Add the green beans in the last 5 minutes, then let the pot sit off the heat for 15 minutes, which is when the potatoes actually drink up the broth.
head_steps: Slice the turkey breast thin and cut the potatoes, carrots, and onion into chunks.
Sear the turkey in vegetable oil, then add the onion wedges.
Add potatoes and carrots with chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.
Cover with a parchment lid and simmer 25 to 30 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the turkey reaches 165F.
Add the green beans in the last 5 minutes and rest off the heat 15 minutes.
Portion by weight into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We cost 1.25 tbsp salt and 0.75 tbsp black pepper but no step ever salts, peppers, or says 'season' anywhere in the recipe.

name: Johnny Marzetti Casserole
ingredients: Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 26.5 oz dry (749 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 7.25 oz (208 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the egg noodles two minutes short of the package time, drain, and set aside. They finish cooking in the oven.
Brown the ground beef and ground pork with the diced onion in your big pot over medium-high heat until no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add the diced bell peppers and sliced mushrooms and cook 5 minutes until they soften.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, brown sugar, dijon, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes so the sauce thickens up.
Fold in the noodles, olives, and half the cheddar until everything is coated.
Spread into a greased 9x13 pan (it will be full) or two smaller pans, top with the rest of the cheddar, and bake at 350 F for about 20 minutes until bubbly and melted.
head_steps: Boil egg noodles two minutes short of package time and drain.
Brown ground beef and pork with onion, then drain fat.
Cook peppers and mushrooms until soft, then add tomatoes, brown sugar, dijon, and seasonings and simmer 10 minutes.
Fold in noodles, olives, and half the cheddar.
Top with remaining cheddar and bake at 350 F for 20 minutes until bubbly.
Cool and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: 3.7 cans (1562 g) of tomato sauce are costed but the sauce step stirs in only diced tomatoes, brown sugar, dijon and garlic powder; the source (theseasonedmom) builds its sauce from tomatoes PLUS two cans of condensed tomato soup, so the dish as written loses roughly half its sauce liquid.

name: John Wayne Casserole
ingredients: Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 1.2 cans (139 g)
Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 1.2 cans (347 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 12.25 oz (346 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Press the biscuit dough into a greased 9x13 pan (plus a small second pan if needed) to form a solid crust, and bake at 350 F for about 10 minutes so it sets.
Brown the ground beef with most of the diced onion in your pot until no pink remains, then drain. Stir in the taco seasoning with a splash of water.
Add the diced tomatoes with green chilies and the diced green chiles. Simmer 5 minutes until thick.
In a bowl, mix the sour cream, mayonnaise, half the cheddar, and the remaining onion.
Layer beef over the biscuit crust, add the bell pepper, spread the sour cream mixture on top, and finish with the rest of the cheddar.
Bake at 350 F for 20 to 25 minutes until the cheese is melted and the edges bubble.
head_steps: Press biscuit dough into a greased 9x13 pan and par-bake at 350 F for 10 minutes.
Brown beef with onion, drain, and stir in taco seasoning, tomatoes with green chilies, and green chiles.
Mix sour cream, mayo, half the cheddar, and remaining onion.
Layer beef, bell pepper, and the creamy mixture over the crust, then top with cheddar.
Bake at 350 F for 20 to 25 minutes until melted and bubbly.
Cut into 14 squares and portion.

findings.detail: We cost 1.25 tbsp salt and 0.5 tbsp pepper but the steps never use them or say 'season' (the source recipe does not call for them either).

name: Kharcho (Georgian Beef and Walnut Rice Soup)
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.5 tbsp (3 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into small cubes and simmer them in salted water for about 75 minutes, skimming the foam, until tender. Keep the broth in the pot.
In a separate pan, cook the chopped onion in the vegetable oil until soft and just golden.
Grind the walnuts to a coarse paste. A food processor is easiest, but a bag and a rolling pin works.
Stir the onions, ground walnuts, and diced tomatoes into the beef pot along with the coriander, cloves, cayenne, and garam masala.
Add the rice and simmer gently 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is tender and the soup has thickened.
Stir in the minced garlic, the red wine vinegar, and the dried dill and cook 3 more minutes.
Kill the heat, fold in the chopped cilantro, and taste for salt. Kharcho should be tangy, so add vinegar before you add salt.
head_steps: Simmer cubed chuck roast in salted water about 75 minutes until tender.
Cook the onion in oil until golden and grind the walnuts to a coarse paste.
Stir onions, walnuts, tomatoes, and spices into the beef pot.
Add the rice and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until thickened.
Finish with garlic, vinegar, dill, and cilantro, then portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: 0.5 tbsp is costed as our stand-in for the source's Aleppo pepper (part of the walnut spice paste), but our spice step adds only coriander, cloves, cayenne and garam masala - the flakes are never used.
0.25 tbsp black pepper is costed (it is in the source's spice blend) but our steps never use it; the finish step says only 'taste for salt'.

name: Korean Beef Bibimbap Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 5.25 cups dry rice with water per your rice cooker or pot method.
Whisk the sauce: gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, and sesame oil.
Brown the ground beef in your big pot over medium-high until no pink remains, then drain. Stir in the sugar-free maple syrup, garlic powder, and half the sauce, and simmer 3 minutes.
Shred the carrots and thin-slice the cucumbers. Toss the cucumbers with a pinch of salt so they stay crisp in the fridge.
Fry or soft-scramble the 14 eggs. For meal prep that keeps, cook the yolks through.
Build each bowl: rice, beef, carrots, cucumber, one egg, a drizzle of the remaining sauce, and a sprinkle of green onion and sesame seeds.
head_steps: Cook the rice.
Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, and sesame oil into a sauce.
Brown the beef, drain, then simmer with syrup, garlic powder, and half the sauce.
Shred carrots, slice and salt the cucumbers, and cook the eggs through.
Assemble 14 bowls: rice, beef, vegetables, egg, remaining sauce, green onion, and sesame seeds.

findings.detail: 0.5 tbsp black pepper is costed but no step uses it (salt is used on the cucumbers; pepper appears nowhere).

name: Korean Braised Chicken and Potatoes (Dakdoritang)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.75 lb (3500 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 9.75 tbsp (52 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, mirin, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, red pepper flakes, and black pepper into a sauce. Taste it and decide how hot you want the week to be, because this is your only chance to adjust.
Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces and toss them with about half the sauce.
Cut the potatoes and carrots into big chunks. Small pieces will disappear into the sauce over a long braise, and you want them to stay recognizable.
Put the chicken, potatoes, carrots, and onion into a wide heavy pot, pour the rest of the sauce over, and add the chicken broth. It should come about halfway up, not cover everything.
Bring it to a boil, then drop to a low simmer, cover, and cook 25 minutes.
Uncover, add the jalapeno, and simmer another 15 to 20 minutes while the liquid reduces into a thick glossy sauce. Stir gently so the potatoes stay whole.
Scatter the green onions over the top off the heat.
head_steps: Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, honey, mirin, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and pepper flakes into a sauce.
Toss the cut chicken thighs with half the sauce.
Add chicken, potatoes, carrots, and onion to a wide pot with the rest of the sauce and the broth.
Simmer covered 25 minutes, then uncover, add jalapeno, and reduce 15 to 20 minutes.
Top with green onions, then weigh the pot and divide into 14 containers.

findings.detail: 1.25 tbsp (24 g) salt is costed but no step uses salt - the sauce, braise and finish are all seasoned from soy/gochujang only, matching the source which calls for no plain salt.

name: Korean Gochujang Ground Pork Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 2 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Stir the sauce together: gochujang, mirin, sugar, soy sauce, and half the sesame oil.
Brown the ground pork in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Drain if needed.
Add the diced onion, garlic, and ginger and cook 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 5 minutes until it glazes the pork and thickens slightly.
Finish with the rest of the sesame oil, most of the green onions, and the toasted sesame seeds. Serve over the rice with the last of the green onions on top.
head_steps: Cook the rice.
Stir together gochujang, mirin, sugar, soy sauce, and half the sesame oil.
Brown the ground pork, then cook with onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the sauce and simmer until it glazes the pork.
Finish with sesame oil, green onions, and sesame seeds, then serve over rice in 14 bowls.

findings.detail: 1.25 tbsp salt and 0.5 tbsp pepper are costed but the steps never use them or say 'season' (the source recipe has neither).

name: Korean Ground Beef Rice Bowls
ingredients: Roasted Red Peppers (generic): 3 oz, from a jar (300 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1 tsp (8 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it apart, then drain the grease.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, and brown sugar and stir into a glossy sauce.
Toss in the broccoli florets and cook until just tender.
Cook the rice while the skillet simmers.
Pile the beef and broccoli over the rice and serve.
head_steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it apart, then drain the grease.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, and brown sugar and stir into a glossy sauce.
Toss in the broccoli florets and cook until just tender.
Cook the rice while the skillet simmers.
Pile the beef and broccoli over the rice and serve.

findings.detail: 3 oz of jarred roasted red peppers are costed; the source (masonfit) stirs them into the beef mid-browning, but our steps never mention them.
1 tsp crushed red pepper is costed; the source whisks it into the gochujang sauce, but our sauce step lists only gochujang, soy, sesame oil and brown sugar.

name: Korean Ground Turkey Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/4 tsp crushed (2 g)
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook until fragrant, about a minute.
Add the teriyaki sauce and honey and let it simmer so the turkey soaks up the glaze.
Steam or microwave the broccoli florets until just tender and fold them in.
Serve over cooked white rice with the sauce spooned on top.
head_steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook until fragrant, about a minute.
Add the teriyaki sauce and honey and let it simmer so the turkey soaks up the glaze.
Steam or microwave the broccoli florets until just tender and fold them in.
Serve over cooked white rice with the sauce spooned on top.

findings.detail: Costed but never used; the source (nutritiontofit) whisks 2 tsp sesame oil into the sauce, while our steps build the glaze from teriyaki and honey only.
Costed but never used; it is a source sauce component (1/4 tsp) that our steps silently drop - same General Tso pattern.
Costed but never used; it is a source sauce component (1/4 tsp) that our steps silently drop.

name: Korean Turkey Japchae
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the Korean glass noodles (dangmyeon) for 6 to 7 minutes until springy, drain them, rinse them cold, and cut through the pile a few times with scissors so they are eatable with a fork.
Beat the eggs, cook them thin in an oiled pan like a flat omelet, slide it out, and slice it into ribbons for the top.
Whisk the sauce: soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and the minced garlic. Set it aside where you can reach it.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pan and brown the ground turkey, breaking it up, until it is cooked through to 165F, then move it to a bowl.

Stir-fry the vegetables in stages so each one keeps its own texture: mushrooms first, then onion and carrot, then red bell pepper, then the thawed and squeezed spinach. Move each batch to the bowl as it finishes.
Return everything to the pan with the noodles, pour the sauce over, and toss over medium heat for 3 minutes until the noodles turn dark and glossy and every strand is coated.
Kill the heat, fold in the green onions, and move it into your weighed pot.
head_steps: Boil the Korean glass noodles 6 to 7 minutes, rinse cold, and cut them shorter.
Cook the beaten eggs into a thin omelet and slice into ribbons.
Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and garlic into a sauce.
Brown the ground turkey to 165F, then stir-fry the mushrooms, onion, carrot, pepper, and spinach in stages.
Toss everything with the noodles and sauce over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Fold in green onions, portion by weight into 14 containers, and top with egg ribbons.

findings.detail: 1 tbsp salt and 0.5 tbsp pepper are costed but no step uses them or says 'season' (the source at least salts the spinach lightly; our spinach step does not).

name: Loaded Beef Taco Skillet Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 6 cans (2366 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (500 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 2 bags (280 g)
Red Bell Pepper (generic): 1/2 cup diced (260 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/4 tsp (2 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (3 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Stir in the chili powder to season the meat.
Add the black beans, corn, diced zucchini, and tomato sauce and simmer until the zucchini is tender.
Stir in a little cooked rice to round out the skillet.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the top and let it melt.
Spoon into bowls and serve.
head_steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Stir in the chili powder to season the meat.
Add the black beans, corn, diced zucchini, and tomato sauce and simmer until the zucchini is tender.
Stir in a little cooked rice to round out the skillet.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the top and let it melt.
Spoon into bowls and serve.

findings.detail: 280 g of diced onion is costed; the source (wholesomemadeeasy) sautes it with the bell pepper, but our steps never mention onion at all.
260 g of diced red bell pepper is costed; the source sautes it in step 2, but our steps never mention it.

findings.ingredient: Ground Cumin, Garlic Powder, Dried Oregano, Paprika, Salt, Red Pepper Flakes, Black Pepper
findings.detail: The source sprinkles its full seasoning set (chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, oregano, paprika, salt, red pepper flakes, black pepper) over the meat in one step; our steps use only the chili powder, silently dropping the other seven costed seasonings.
2 tsp oil is costed (the source browns the meat and vegetables in it) but our steps never mention oil.

name: Massaman Beef Curry with Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dried arbol chiles in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend them with the onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro stems, and lemongrass paste into a smooth curry paste.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste over medium heat until it darkens and the raw smell burns off, about 8 minutes.
Add the ground cloves, cumin, nutmeg, garam masala, and cinnamon and toast for 30 seconds, then stir in the thick top layer of the coconut milk and let it bubble until the oil starts to separate.
Add the beef cut into large cubes and turn it in the paste, then pour in the beef broth and remaining coconut milk with the bay leaves. Bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook on low for about 2 hours, until the beef is tender enough to cut with the side of a spoon.

Add the potatoes in chunks and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes more, then season with the fish sauce, sugar, and lime juice. Massaman should taste salty, sweet, and sour all at once, so adjust until all three are there.
Cook the rice, then stir the chopped peanuts into the curry off the heat.
head_steps: Soak the dried chiles, then blend them with onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro, and lemongrass into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil until dark, toast the dry spices, then cook the thick coconut milk until the oil separates.
Add the cubed beef, broth, and remaining coconut milk and simmer covered about 2 hours.
Add the potatoes and simmer 30 minutes, then season with fish sauce, sugar, and lime juice.
Stir in the peanuts, cook the rice, and portion both into 14 containers.

findings.detail: 1 tbsp salt and 0.5 tbsp pepper are costed but the steps season only with fish sauce, sugar and lime juice and never mention salt or pepper.

name: Massaman Chicken Curry
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 2.75 lb (1270 g)
Red Curry Paste (Thai Kitchen): 11.25 oz (318 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Spoon the thick cream off the top of the unshaken coconut milk cans into your largest pot, keeping the thin liquid aside. Cook it with the olive oil over medium-high for 3 to 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the curry paste and the diced onion and fry them in that oil for 3 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens and smells toasted.
Add the chicken cut into chunks along with the garlic and grated ginger, and turn everything until coated.
Pour in the reserved coconut liquid, then add the cubed potatoes and sliced carrots. Bring it to a simmer.
Stir in the peanut butter, brown sugar and fish sauce, then simmer uncovered 30 to 35 minutes until the potatoes are fork tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened around them.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice, tasting as you go. Massaman should read sweet first, salty second and sour last, in that order.
Fold in most of the chopped peanuts and the cilantro, holding some of each back to scatter on top.
head_steps: Fry the thick coconut cream with oil until it splits, then fry the curry paste and onion 3 minutes.
Add the chunked chicken, garlic and ginger and coat in the paste.
Add the reserved coconut liquid, potatoes and carrots and bring to a simmer.
Stir in peanut butter, brown sugar and fish sauce and simmer uncovered 30 to 35 minutes until thick.
Finish with lime juice, chopped peanuts and cilantro, then portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: 1 tbsp salt and 0.5 tbsp pepper are costed but no step uses them; seasoning is done via fish sauce, brown sugar and lime, matching the source which lists no salt/pepper.

name: Mediterranean Ground Turkey Bowls
ingredients: Black Pepper (Great Value): 1/4 tsp cracked (2 g)
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Add the chopped onion and sliced zucchini and cook until tender.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and let it simmer a few minutes to come together.
Season with salt, pepper, and whatever dried herbs you like, then take it off the heat.
Serve over cooked white rice with a big dollop of Greek yogurt on top.
head_steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Add the chopped onion and sliced zucchini and cook until tender.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and let it simmer a few minutes to come together.
Season with salt, pepper, and whatever dried herbs you like, then take it off the heat.
Serve over cooked white rice with a big dollop of Greek yogurt on top.

findings.detail: 1050 g of cucumber is costed (the source tops each bowl with chopped cucumber) but our steps never mention cucumber anywhere.
2 minced cloves are costed (the source cooks minced garlic into the turkey) but our steps never use garlic.
Costed for the source's garlic-dill yogurt sauce, but our steps serve a plain dollop of Greek yogurt and never use lemon juice.
Both are costed as components of the source's yogurt sauce, which our steps never build; the only step reference is a vague 'whatever dried herbs you like', which cannot cover garlic powder.

name: Middle Eastern Beef Kofta Bowls with Tzatziki
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.5 tbsp (3 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the tzatziki: grate about a third of the cucumbers, salt them, and squeeze out the water hard. Stir into the Greek yogurt with half the garlic, a splash of lemon juice, the mint, and a pinch of salt. Refrigerate.
Cook the rice: 4.5 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Grate one of the red onions and squeeze it dry. Mix it into the ground beef with the remaining garlic, cumin, cinnamon, allspice, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper.
Shape the beef into small logs or ovals, about 3 per serving, and set them on foil-lined sheet pans.
Broil or bake at 450 F for 12 to 15 minutes, flipping once, until browned outside and cooked through with no pink in the center.
Slice the remaining cucumber and red onion and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Build each bowl: rice, kofta, tomato and cucumber salad, cilantro on top, tzatziki in its own corner or cup.
head_steps: Make tzatziki: squeeze grated salted cucumber dry, then mix with Greek yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, and mint. Chill.
Cook the rice.
Mix beef with squeezed grated onion, garlic, and the spices, then shape into small logs.
Broil or bake at 450 F for 12 to 15 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Assemble 14 bowls with rice, kofta, tomato cucumber salad, cilantro, and tzatziki on the side.

findings.detail: 2.25 tbsp olive oil is costed; the source (slenderkitchen) stirs olive oil into the tzatziki, but our tzatziki step lists only yogurt, cucumber, garlic, lemon, mint and salt, and no other step uses oil.
0.75 tbsp is costed; the source's tzatziki includes 1/2 tsp oregano, but our steps never use oregano anywhere.

name: Million Dollar Baked Spaghetti
ingredients: 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 5.5 oz (159 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 11.25 oz (316 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti two minutes short of package time and drain.
Brown the ground beef and hot Italian sausage together in your big pot until no pink remains, then drain. Stir in the marinara and Italian seasoning and simmer 5 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, softened cream cheese, and sour cream in a bowl until smooth.
Layer in a greased 9x13 pan: half the spaghetti, all the cheese mixture, the rest of the spaghetti, then all the meat sauce.
Top with the mozzarella and bake at 350 F for 25 to 30 minutes until melted and bubbling at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting so the layers hold.
head_steps: Boil spaghetti two minutes short of package time and drain.
Brown beef and sausage, drain, then simmer with marinara and Italian seasoning.
Mix ricotta, cream cheese, and sour cream until smooth.
Layer spaghetti, cheese mixture, spaghetti, then meat sauce in a 9x13 pan.
Top with mozzarella and bake at 350 F for 25 to 30 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, cut into 14 squares, and portion.

findings.detail: 1 tbsp salt and 0.5 tbsp pepper are costed but the steps never use them or say 'season' (the source lists neither).

name: Mongolian Ground Beef Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/4 tsp (2 g)
Beef Broth (Great Value): 1/4 cup (or water) (210 g)
Green Onions: 1/4 cup, thinly sliced (40 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks, then drain any grease.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and stir for about a minute.
Pour in the soy sauce and honey and let it bubble into a glaze.
Add the broccoli florets and sliced red pepper and cook until just tender.
Cook the rice while the skillet finishes.
Spoon the saucy beef and vegetables over the rice and serve.
head_steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks, then drain any grease.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and stir for about a minute.
Pour in the soy sauce and honey and let it bubble into a glaze.
Add the broccoli florets and sliced red pepper and cook until just tender.

findings.ingredient: Hoisin Sauce, Sesame Oil, Rice Vinegar, Cornstarch, Beef Broth, Black Pepper, Red Pepper Flakes
findings.detail: All seven are costed and all seven belong to the source's (eatyourselfskinny) whisked sauce plus cornstarch slurry, but our steps build the glaze from soy sauce and honey only - the dish's actual sauce is silently dropped.
1/4 cup sliced green onions is costed; the source stirs them in off the heat, but our steps never mention them.
1 Tbsp is costed (the source browns the beef in it) but our steps never mention oil.

name: Moo Shu Pork Rice Bowls
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 4.75 tbsp (84 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the pork shoulder thin against the grain and toss it with some of the soy sauce, the cornstarch and the black pepper. Let it sit while you prep everything else.
Shred the cabbage, cut the carrots into matchsticks, slice the mushrooms, mince the garlic, and separate the green onion whites from the tops.
Beat the eggs and scramble them in a little of the vegetable oil until just set, then take them out and chop them roughly.
Get your largest pan very hot, add more oil, and stir fry the marinated pork in batches until it is browned and cooked through. Crowding the pan will steam the pork instead of searing it.
Add the garlic and the green onion whites, then the mushrooms, carrots and cabbage, and stir fry until the cabbage wilts but still has some bite left in it.
Return the pork, add the hoisin sauce, oyster sauce, the rest of the soy sauce and the chicken broth, and toss until everything is glazed.
Kill the heat, fold in the scrambled egg and the green onion tops, finish with the sesame oil, and serve over rice with warm tortilla strips standing in for the pancakes.
head_steps: Slice the pork shoulder thin and marinate it in soy sauce, cornstarch and black pepper.
Scramble the beaten eggs in oil, then remove and chop them.
Stir fry the marinated pork in batches in a very hot pan until browned.
Add the garlic, green onion whites, mushrooms, carrots and cabbage and stir fry until the cabbage wilts.
Return the pork, glaze with hoisin, oyster sauce, soy sauce and broth, then fold in the egg and finish with sesame oil.

findings.detail: The final step serves the dish 'with warm tortilla strips standing in for the pancakes', but no tortilla appears in the costed ingredient list.
1 tbsp (20 g) salt is costed but no step uses salt; the marinade uses soy/cornstarch/pepper and all later seasoning comes from the sauces.

name: Moussaka (Greek Beef and Eggplant Bake)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Slice the eggplant into thick rounds, salt them, and let them sweat in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat them dry, brush with olive oil, and roast at 425F until soft and golden, about 25 minutes. This step is what keeps moussaka from turning watery.
While the eggplant roasts, cook the onion in olive oil until soft, add the garlic, then brown the ground beef and break it up as it cooks.

Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, sugar, cinnamon, oregano, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Simmer until it thickens and most of the liquid is gone, about 30 minutes. A wet meat sauce makes a sloppy bake.

Make the bechamel. Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook it for two minutes, then add the milk slowly while whisking until it thickens. Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and nutmeg, then temper in the beaten eggs so they do not scramble.
Scatter bread crumbs across the bottom of a large baking dish, then layer roasted eggplant, meat sauce, more eggplant, and pour the bechamel over the top so it reaches every corner.
Bake at 350F for 45 minutes, until the top is set and browned in patches. Let it rest at least 30 minutes before cutting. Cut it hot and the layers slide apart.
Cook the rice while the bake rests and put a scoop in the bottom of each container to round the meal out.
head_steps: Salt, dry, oil, and roast the eggplant slices at 425F until golden.
Brown the beef with onion and garlic, then simmer with tomatoes, paste, broth, and spices until thick.
Make a bechamel from butter, flour, and milk, then finish it with parmesan and tempered eggs.
Layer bread crumbs, eggplant, meat sauce, and eggplant in a large dish and pour the bechamel over the top.
Bake at 350F for 45 minutes and rest 30 minutes before cutting into 14 portions.

findings.detail: 0.06 cups (15 g) of chicken broth is costed - apparently the stand-in for the source's bechamel stock powder - but the bechamel step (and every other step) never uses it.
